Definition: from G4636; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion):-- dwell.
BiblicalUsage: Skenoo means to dwell, to pitch a tent and live in it, and its greatest occurrence is the incarnation itself: the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us. The throne will dwell among the redeemed, and the voice from heaven says God will dwell with men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Word pitching His tent among us is the whole gospel in one verb. God did not visit; He moved in, and I hold that He has never moved out.
